subject: Model fit eval parity discussion - next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan

Hi Alex / Sophie -

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Goal: Understand whether open models can match PayGrid's current baseline for payment instruction extraction and routing decisions.
- Scope: ~2k representative prompts from your production logs (anonymized) + 200 edge-case prompts you highlighted.
- Success criteria: parity defined as <=2% absolute delta on intent classification accuracy and <=5% relative delta on extraction F1 vs your baseline (we can refine).

What we'll do (proposed):
1) Run a model-fit eval comparing 3 open candidates + your baseline: Llama-3-70B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-XL, and Falcon-180B-Inst (llama-style tuned).
2) Use the prompt set attached (paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json) and the evaluation rubric in the attached PDF.
3) Produce a per-prompt CSV, aggregated metrics (accuracy, F1, latency), and a small set of examples where open models regress vs baseline.
4) Recommend next steps (canary deploy, A/B test, or stick with proprietary baseline).

What we need from you:
- A temporary S3 share or dataset link for the anonymized sample (S3/Presigned or GDrive ok).
- Confirmation on acceptance thresholds (as above) or any additional metric you care about (e.g., rerank recall).

Timeline: once we have the sample access, we can run initial evals in ~48-72 hours and share a results deck + CSV.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.json, redwood_eval_instructions.pdf

Next step: Can you confirm you can share the sample and whether the thresholds above look reasonable? Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan

Lauren - thanks for the clear write-up. This matches our internal read. A few quick answers and a question: 

1) We can share a presigned S3 bucket with an anonymized sample - I'll get IT to produce that today. Expect a share link by EOD.
2) Thresholds look reasonable as a starting point. We do want to add: false positive rate on high-risk intents (refunds/chargebacks) should be under 1.5%.
3) Question: for latency numbers are you reporting cold-start inference or steady-state (we care about end-to-end P95 with our infra)?

I can also add Sophie to coordinate data sharing.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations, PayGrid
alex.johnson@paygrid.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed eval plan

Hi Alex / team - looping in some technical details so expectations are clear.

Thanks Lauren for the plan. A few technical notes from the eval side: 
- Metrics: we will produce intent accuracy, extraction F1, false positive rate (per-intent), token-level latency (P50/P95), and cost-per-request estimates using our latency-cost model.
- Sampling: we'll run stratified sampling across your prod buckets (high-frequency, low-frequency, edge cases) and hold out ~10% as a hidden validation set.
- Models: open candidates will be run in quantized modes where supported (q8/q4f16) to reflect realistic cost/latency tradeoffs. We will compare against the PayGrid baseline (your provided scores) and also a Redwood-provisioned tuned baseline where appropriate.
- Regression handling: any prompt where an open model drops below baseline by more than the thresholds will be flagged for manual review - we'll provide 100 representative regression examples.
- Acceptance: If core intent accuracy is within the delta and high-risk false positive <1.5%, we recommend pilot canarying with a 10% traffic A/B for 2 weeks.

Data access: Alex - presigned S3 is perfect. Please include a README with schema and an examples.jsonl file; we need the ground-truth labels for scoring.

Timeline: once we have S3 access, expect an initial results package in ~72 hours. If you want us to run an expanded run (all 20k prompts) that's an extra 3-5 days.

I've attached the eval run config we use (eval-run-config.yaml) - it contains the exact model variants, batch sizes, and quantization flags we'll use. A few points to note for PayGrid ops: quantized runs will alter perf but generally give 2-3x throughput improvements at small quality cost; we'll surface per-prompt deltas.

If helpful, Aditya can run a quick parity check on a 200-sample subset first and share an interim note.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead ML Engineer, Model Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: eval-run-config.yaml
